You have the right to seek mental health support, regardless of your husband's wishes. Your well-being matters, and accessing care is your personal decision.

Regarding privacy: mental health providers are bound by confidentiality laws and cannot share your information with anyone, including your spouse, without your written consent. However, insurance can be more complicated. If you're on a shared insurance plan, Explanation of Benefits (EOB) statements may be sent to the primary policyholder, which could include general information about services used. You can call your insurance company directly and ask about their privacy options—some plans offer alternative communication methods or allow you to request confidential communications.

If you're concerned about safety or feel pressured in ways that worry you, consider reaching out to a domestic violence hotline (1-800-799-7233) to talk through your situation confidentially. They can help you think through your options safely.

You deserve support, and there are people who can help you navigate this.
